clue.text: Trade in continent

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay: POTTY is a crazy, anagram-style signal and TRAINED is the fodder, which rearranges to spell these two clue words

explanation.surface: A short note about commerce being done somewhere on a continent such as Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'potty' (crazy) works as an anagram signal, and TRAINED made potty gives TRADE IN. 'Continent' is not a landmass but the adjective for control over the bladder.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who is potty-trained has learned bladder and bowel control, which is what being continent means.

clue.text: Cubs cycling through Oregon drug complex

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: OR is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Oregon

indicators.note: cycling sends the first letter of the word Cubs round to its end

parts.note: E is the usual shorthand for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Young scouts on a trip through Oregon stumble into a drug-making complex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' moves the C of CUBS to the end, giving BSCU, which goes 'through' OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure is hard to understand, as anything intricate or complicated tends to be.

clue.text: Time Telstar broadcast what Hollywood produces?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the word Telstar has its letters strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Telstar, the communications satellite, transmitting the sort of output Hollywood is famous for.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: Hollywood turns out starlets, and the question mark hints at little 'tarts' in a teasing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartlets are small tarts, and the question mark jokes that Hollywood churns out young starlets, unkindly dubbed tarts.

clue.text: Third eye oddly substantial

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters across the words Third eye

explanation.surface: A mystical third eye that is strangely solid and real.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidy sum is a large one, so tidy can mean considerable or substantial in amount.

clue.text: First to replace middle of song in poet, Owen's sort of rhyme gets help

indicators.note: to replace tells us one string of letters is swapped out for another inside the longer word

parts.note: the war poet Wilfred Owen was known for half-rhymes built on assonance

indicators.note: the middle of the word song is its two central letters

parts.note: First is written 1ST, read as IST

explanation.surface: A poet working Wilfred Owen's style of rhyme into a song gets some help with it.
explanation.walkthrough: In ASSONANCE the middle of 'song', ON, is replaced by IST (First written as 1ST), giving ASSISTANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance is aid or support given to someone, exactly what help is as a noun.

clue.text: In part, Dubya wrong about country

indicators.note: about signals that the letters picked out are read in the opposite direction
In part means only a portion of the words Dubya wrong is used

explanation.surface: George W Bush (Dubya) was partly wrong about some country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' finds YAWRON within dubYA WRONg; 'about' turns it round to NORWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a Scandinavian nation, one example of a country.

clue.text: Singer and model paired over a beer

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: dual means paired or twofold
IPA, India pale ale, is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A singer and a model pair up over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: DUAL then IPA, read together as the name DUA LIPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dua Lipa is a British pop star who has also worked as a fashion model.

clue.text: I see cop baffled before robber returns carrying scrap of gold and silver

indicators.note: before places the first part ahead of the next
baffled means confused, so the words I see cop are jumbled
carrying means the robber word holds another piece inside it
returns means the letters that follow are read backwards

parts.note: a thief is a robber

indicators.note: a scrap of the word gold is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A policeman, foxed, watches a robber come back holding a little gold and silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baffled' scrambles the policeman phrase; 'returns' turns the robber word into FEIHT, and 'carrying' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of eight were Spanish silver dollars, the coins of pirate stories, so they are silver coinage.

clue.text: Not much in clothes shop — changed into thong

parts.note: Next is a British high-street clothing chain

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters of into thong are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in a clothes shop changes into a thong, wearing not much at all.
explanation.walkthrough: NEXT is a UK clothing retailer. 'Changed' rearranges INTO THONG into TONOTHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Next to nothing is an idiom for a tiny amount, almost none at all.

clue.text: In seconds, posh wine is protected

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
red is wine by colour

explanation.surface: Within seconds the fancy wine has been made safe.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class or posh is a crossword staple, from the 1950s U and non-U usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Being insured means covered against loss by a policy, so financially protected.

clue.text: Farmer, say, succeeded spreading manure

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

indicators.note: spreading means scattered about, so the letters of manure move around

explanation.surface: A farmer did well by spreading muck on the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Farmer' looks like a job, but it is a family name, an example of a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmer is also a family name, so it is one example of a surname.

clue.text: Join revolution before the French

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: a coup is a sudden seizure of power, a revolution
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An invitation to take part in an uprising ahead of the French.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple is to link or connect two things, the verb sense of join.

clue.text: Some articles say I stalked writer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A writer confesses in print that they followed someone obsessively.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayist composes essays, so is one kind of author.

clue.text: Rod's witchcraft?

parts.note: craft is read as a vehicle: the long pole a witch flies on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Witchcraft' looks like sorcery, but read it as a witch's craft, the aircraft she rides, which is just a rod with bristles.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch traditionally flies on a besom, a rod with twigs, so it is her flying craft.

clue.text: Offal soup's first, then we film sitcom

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the word soup's

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's film E.T.
Bread was a long-running BBC sitcom set in Liverpool

explanation.surface: A menu of offal with soup to start, then we watch a film and a sitcom.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread was a 1980s BBC sitcom about a Liverpool family.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetbread is the culinary name for the thymus or pancreas, a kind of offal.

clue.text: Film villain has nothing on corona

parts.note: HAL is the murderous computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A movie baddie with nothing to say about the corona.
explanation.definitionFit: A corona is a ring of light around a body, as is a halo.

clue.text: Suffers hard in test for promotion

indicators.note: in places the suffering and hard pieces within the test word

parts.note: the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for vehicles
ails means suffers
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone struggles hard in an exam for a promotion at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the yearly safety test that British cars must pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A mailshot is a batch of advertising letters, a form of marketing promotion.

clue.text: Pert, following kiss

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
to lip is an old word for to kiss

explanation.surface: A cheeky person coming after a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Flip is short for flippant, meaning cheeky or saucy, the same sense as pert.

clue.text: Incomplete arrest following one northern copper's nightmare

indicators.note: following places the arrest piece after the others

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: Incomplete means the arrest word loses its final letter

parts.note: a bust is an arrest

explanation.surface: A northern policeman's bad dream: a botched arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but here it is the metal, symbol Cu. 'Incomplete' cuts BUST to BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is a demon believed to lie on sleepers, and by extension a nightmare.

clue.text: Narrow escape when bird bites husband and dog runs free

indicators.note: bites means the bird word closes round another piece

parts.note: a toucan is a big-billed tropical bird

indicators.note: runs free means loose, so the letters of dog are rearranged

explanation.surface: A close shave when a bird pecks a man and his dog bolts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bites' puts H in TOUCAN. 'Runs free' turns DOG into DGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch and go describes a risky situation whose outcome is uncertain, a close call.

clue.text: Best in The Beatles, once?

parts.note: Best is the surname of Pete Best, who played in the early Beatles

explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like praise of the top Beatle, but it is Pete Best, the band's original percussionist before Ringo Starr.
explanation.definitionFit: Pete Best played drums for the Beatles until 1962, so he was the band's percussionist.

clue.text: Right key starts to unlock everything — salvation!

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each of unlock and everything

explanation.surface: The correct key opens everything, a moment of deliverance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescue is a saving from danger, the same thing as salvation.

clue.text: Appreciate fashionable pleat

parts.note: in means fashionable
a crease is a fold, like a pleat

explanation.surface: Admire a stylish pleat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appreciate' looks like 'value', but here it means rise in value.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets that appreciate grow in value, so to appreciate is to grow or rise.

clue.text: Work from Poet Laureate: four letters, having eight rhymes

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for Poet Laureate
the letter group OUGH has about eight pronunciations, as in through, cough, bough, though

explanation.surface: A poem by the Poet Laureate in a rhyme scheme of four letters with eight rhymes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ending OUGH famously has many pronunciations, so it rhymes in eight different ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To plough on is to toil steadily, so plough means labour as a verb.

clue.text: Pass is in Virginia

indicators.note: in puts the word is within the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: A permit is being held in Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official permit to enter a country, a travel pass.

clue.text: Most of his meat not on this uncovered grill

indicators.note: Most of means the word his loses its last letter
not means the word on is removed from the meat

parts.note: bacon is a meat

indicators.note: uncovered means the word this loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Most of his meat isn't cooked on this open grill.
explanation.walkthrough: HI, then BACON without ON (BAC), then HI from tHIs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hibachi is a small Japanese charcoal brazier used for cooking, a type of barbecue.

clue.text: Cruel chums stripped man naked in pub

indicators.note: in places the stripped pieces within the pub word

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: stripped means the word chums loses its outer letters
naked means the word man is stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: Cruel friends strip a man naked in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripped' and 'naked' both mean losing the outer letters, leaving HUM and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhuman behaviour lacks compassion, so it is brutal and unkind.

clue.text: The gutless star karate chopped raw meat

indicators.note: chopped means cut up, so the letters are rearranged
gutless means the word The loses its middle letter

explanation.surface: A cowardly star chopped with a karate blow.
explanation.walkthrough: TE from 'The gutless', with STAR and KARATE, rearranges to STEAKTARTARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak tartare is minced beef served uncooked, a dish of raw beef.
